national.headline: Government Defends Referendum for New Provinces
national.line: Information Minister Attaullah Tarar described holding a referendum as a constitutional and legal method to gauge public opinion on carving out new provinces.

national.headline: PTA Approves In-Flight Internet Licensing Framework
national.line: The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority approved a regulatory framework enabling satellite-based internet and mobile connectivity aboard commercial flights.

national.headline: Punjab Local Polls Set in Two Phases
national.line: The Election Commission of Pakistan agreed to hold local government elections in Punjab in two phases starting in February.

national.headline: Pakistan and Turkmenistan to Convene TAPI Meeting
national.line: Pakistan and Turkmenistan agreed to convene the steering committee for the TAPI gas pipeline project to enhance regional energy cooperation.

national.headline: ADB Approves $500m Loan for Pension Reforms
national.line: The Asian Development Bank approved a 500 million dollar loan to help Pakistan reform its federal civil service pension system.

national.headline: Saudi Firm Explores $30bn Energy Investment
national.line: Saudi Arabia's Delta Energy plans to evaluate a 30 billion dollar energy investment, including an assessment of a natural gas pipeline to Gwadar.

national.headline: BISP Expands Coverage to Unmarried Older Women
national.line: The Benazir Income Support Programme approved the inclusion of unmarried women aged 45 and older in its social safety net.

international.headline: US Proposes Tighter Rules for Work Green Cards
international.line: The US Labour Department proposed tighter rules requiring employers to demonstrate greater efforts to hire domestic workers before sponsoring foreign employees.

international.headline: UK Sanctions Israeli Settlement Builders
international.line: Britain sanctioned eight Israeli firms involved in planning and constructing West Bank settlements to protect prospects for a two-state solution.

international.headline: UN Court to Rule on Myanmar Rohingya Genocide
international.line: The International Court of Justice prepared to issue a verdict on whether Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority in 2017.

international.headline: Trump Attends Quad Summit in Manila
international.line: US President Donald Trump began an Asian diplomatic tour in Manila, joining the first Quad leaders' meeting held in two years.

international.headline: Ukrainian Strike Damages Crimean Bridge
international.line: A Ukrainian attack caused the main road arch of the Crimean bridge to collapse into the sea, severing a key transport link.

international.headline: US and Russia Oppose Autonomous Weapons Limits
international.line: The United States and Russia are set to oppose binding global negotiations in Geneva regulating artificial intelligence in autonomous weapons systems.

international.headline: Iran Bars Nuclear Inspectors Until War Ends
international.line: Tehran announced it will block UN nuclear inspectors from visiting damaged atomic sites until the current military war concludes.
